line: Hallo. This is Liam, in for Bear. One name, three places you meet it. A chat that thinks with you. A coder that ships with you. A teammate that takes the whole task. This film is the map.
screen: Hook card reading 'one name, three places you meet it?' Three boxes labeled 'chat', 'code', 'teammate' slide in side by side.

line: Three terms before we start. Conversation: Claude in chat — you talk, it answers. Claude Code: the coding agent, living in your terminal. Cowork: the teammate — you delegate the outcome, it does the work. Keep those three in your pocket.
screen: Three term cards appear one by one: 'Conversation — Claude in chat, you talk, it answers' / 'Claude Code — the coding agent, living in your terminal' / 'Cowork — the teammate, you delegate the outcome, it does the work'.

line: First surface: conversation. Claude in chat — the app, the website. You ask, it answers. It's where you think out loud: questions, drafts, decisions. The fastest way to meet Claude, and for most people, the first.
screen: Chat card labeled 'chat': a question bubble appears, then an answer bubble. Caption: 'thinks with you'.

line: Second surface: Claude Code. It lives where the code lives — the terminal, the editor, the desktop app. It reads your repo, writes the code, runs the tests, opens the pull request. Cat Woo, who leads the product, states its mission in one line: bridge the difference between an idea and a shipped product.
screen: Terminal window card labeled 'code': a prompt line appears, then code lines, then a check mark. Quote chip: 'bridge the difference between an idea and a shipped product — Cat Woo'.

line: Third surface: Cowork. Not a chat, not a terminal — a teammate. You hand it the outcome, not the steps. Then it works while you're away. Angela Jang, who leads the platform, names the difference: a harness gives the model tools, an environment, and the permission to act. It doesn't just tell you about the fix — it makes it happen.
screen: Task card labeled 'teammate': an arrow 'you hand over the outcome' points into the card; inside, small task rows check off. Quote chip: 'it doesn't just tell you about the fix — it makes it happen — Angela Jang'.

line: Where does chat win? Thinking. A question with no clean answer, a draft that needs a second mind, a decision you want to argue out. It's instant, it's conversational, and it never touches your files. When you do the doing and Claude advises — that's chat.
screen: Thought bubble: three question marks collapse into one answer line. Label: 'thinks with you'.

line: Where does Code win? Building. The repo is its home turf. It reads the code, writes the code, runs the tests. At Spotify, a background agent built on the same kit opens the pull requests — over a thousand a month, and migration time down ninety percent. When the doing is code, Code does it.
screen: Code file card labeled 'builds in your repo': lines appear with check marks. Stat chips: '1,000+ PRs a month', 'migration time −90%'.

line: Where does Cowork win? Owning. Multi-step work with a finish line: research the account, draft the brief, schedule the follow-up. At Rakuten, one product manager coordinates teams of agents the way a leader manages teams of humans — and major releases ship every two weeks instead of once a quarter. You set the outcome; it runs the errands.
screen: Outcome card labeled 'owns the outcome': a progress bar fills while three task rows check off. Caption: 'while you're away'.

line: So which Claude for which task? One question decides: who does the doing? If you do the doing and Claude advises — chat. If the doing is code — Claude Code. If you hand over the whole outcome — Cowork. Three surfaces, one question.
screen: Decision card: 'who does the doing?' Three branches: 'you do it → chat' / 'the doing is code → Claude Code' / 'hand over the outcome → Cowork'.

line: And the mistakes, so you can skip them. Don't delegate to chat — it can advise, but it can't act. Don't brainstorm in Code — it's a builder, not a sounding board. And don't hand Cowork a vague wish — it needs the outcome, not the steps. Right surface, right job.
screen: Three crossed-out pairings with red X marks: 'delegate → chat: it can't act' / 'brainstorm → Code: it's a builder' / 'vague wish → Cowork: needs the outcome'.

line: Here's the part people miss: the three stack. One task can touch all three. Think it through in chat, build it in Code, hand the rollout to Cowork. The handoff between them is the skill — and it's the subject of this whole series.
screen: Three boxes chained with arrows: 'chat' → 'Code' → 'Cowork'. One task token travels the chain.

line: This isn't our invention. At Anthropic's Tokyo keynote, Cat Woo closed the day with the same picture: the models, the platform agents, and Claude Code — her words — three layers to one story. One assistant. Three places you meet it. Now you know which door to knock on.
screen: Quote card: 'three layers to one story' — Cat Woo, Anthropic Tokyo keynote.

line: And this series walks the map in order. Next film: Delegate It — we hand Cowork its first real task and steer it mid-flight. Then scheduled tasks, tagging Claude into your team channel, the verification loop, all the way to the AI-native company. Ten films. This was the map. The walking starts now.
screen: Series map card: ten dots in a row, the first highlighted; caption 'Next: Delegate It'.

line: Let's recap. Chat thinks with you — you do the doing. Code builds in your repo — the doing is code. Cowork owns delegated outcomes — you hand over the finish line. One question picks the surface: who does the doing?
screen: Recap card. Four lines appear one by one: 'Chat: thinks with you — you do the doing' / 'Code: builds in your repo — the doing is code' / 'Cowork: owns outcomes — you hand over the finish line' / 'One question: who does the doing?'

line: Your turn. Pick one real task on your list — something small, something this week. Ask the one question: who does the doing? Write down which Claude gets it, and why. Then check: did the surface match the job?
screen: Your-turn card: 'Pick one task. Ask: who does the doing?' Below it: 'Which Claude gets it — and why?'
